shots.caption: Paris-Greenwich 1888, Clock Error: meaning of each column in the transit tables
shots.quote: Column 5 gives, in all cases, the time of transit over the middle wire, set at the reading of the R.A. micrometer adopted for the day, corrected for parallax of pens. Column 6 gives the transit corrected for Collimation, Level, and Azimuth Error (p. 62). Column 7 contains the Tabular Apparent R.A. of the stars ... Column 8 shows the difference of columns 6 and 7, which is the Clock Error indicated by the individual stars.

Final 1888 result
shots.quote: Longitude of the Paris instrument East of the Greenwich instrument:- 9m20s·602 ± 0s·018 This longitude refers to the following meridians:- At Paris, the pier of the English instrument which is 0s·27 west of Cassini's meridian. At Greenwich the old meridian of Bradley, 19 ft. or 0s·02 west of the Transit-Circle. Thus the meridian of Cassini is, 9m 20s·60 - 0s·02 + 0s·27 or 9m 20s·85 E. of the Greenwich Transit Circle.
